podcast.body: Released in 1991, this album marked a transitional period for Sting, representing "the last gasp of 80s sting and his jazzy moody melancholy rock." The entire album is deeply personal, abounding with references to death and Sting's childhood, particularly the shipyards he grew up around, following the passing of his father since his previous album. "Indeed, the entire Soul Cages album abounded with references to death and Sting's childhood, including the shipyards he grew up around."
